# Environmics {background-color="#b2bc63"}

## Genotype-by-environment interaction {.custom1}

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
g1 = c(18,20,22,24)
g2 = g1-4

dat = data.frame(
  Valor = c(g1, g2),
  Ambiente = rep(paste0("E",1:length(g1)),2),
  Tratamento = rep(paste0("G", 1:2), each = 4),
  GA = c("Plasticity, No interaction")
)


g1 = c(12,17,22,27)
g2 = c(10, 13, 16, 19)

dat = rbind(dat,
            data.frame(
              Valor = c(g1, g2),
              Ambiente = rep(paste0("E", 1:length(g1)), 2),
              Tratamento = rep(paste0("G", 1:2), each = 4),
              GA = c("Non-crossover interaction")
            ))


g1 = rev(c(12,17,22,27))
g2 = rev(g1)

dat = rbind(dat,
            data.frame(
              Valor = c(g1, g2),
              Ambiente = rep(paste0("E", 1:length(g1)), 2),
              Tratamento = rep(paste0("G", 1:2), each = 4),
              GA = c("Crossover interaction")
            ))

dat$GA = factor(dat$GA, levels = unique(dat$GA))

dat |> ggplot(aes(x = Ambiente, y = Valor, color = Tratamento, shape = Tratamento,
                  linetype = Tratamento)) + 
  geom_point(size = 4) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = Tratamento), linewidth = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(.~GA) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", text = element_text(size = 18))  + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c('#10342d', '#b2bc63')) + 
  labs(x = "Environment", y = "Phenotype", color = "Genotype", shape = "Genotype", linetype = "Genotype")
```

## Environmic marker {.custom1}

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.2em;"}

Adapted from [@marcatti_enviromic_2026]:

:::: incremental

-   [Linearity]{.blue}: The enviromic marker should have a linear relationship with the phenotype, analogous to treating SNPs in linear reaction models
-   [Site potential]{.blue}: A site with a high value for a given enviromic marker (a high envirotype) tends to offer greater potential for expressing the trait
-   [Response heterogeneity]{.blue}: A site favourable for one genotype or group is not necessarily favourable for all
-   [EC-genotype dependence]{.blue}: An EC influential for one genotype may be influential for others, indicating that envirotypic polymorphism does not imply uniformity of genetic response.

::::

:::

# Environmics + Genomics {background-color="#b2bc63"}

## Reaction norm models {.custom1}

Proposed by @jarquin_reaction_2014 to surpass dimensionality issues

. . .

-   Baseline multi-environment GBLUP model:

$$
\bar{\boldsymbol y} = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol Z_1 \boldsymbol e + \boldsymbol Z_2 \boldsymbol g + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

::: incremental

-   $\boldsymbol e \to$ [Fixed]{.red} effect of environment
-   $\boldsymbol g \to$ Random main genetic effect
    -   $\boldsymbol g \sim \mathcal N \left(\boldsymbol 0, \boldsymbol K_g \sigma^2_g\right)$
-   $\varepsilon_{ij} \to$ IID residual

:::

## Reaction norm models {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   **Research question**: How molecular markers interact with environmental covariables?
-   First, are the environments really independent?
-   Environmic kernel:
:::

. . .

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega} = \frac{\boldsymbol{V}\boldsymbol{V}^\prime}{q}
$$

::: incremental
-   $\boldsymbol V \to$ matrix of environmental markers (scaled and centred)
-   $q \to$ number of environmental markers (columns of $\boldsymbol V$)
:::

## Reaction norm models {.custom1}

$$
\bar{\boldsymbol y} = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol Z_1 \boldsymbol \omega + \boldsymbol Z_2 \boldsymbol g + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

-   Environmental covariable main effect: 

$$
\boldsymbol \omega \sim \mathcal N\left(\boldsymbol 0, \boldsymbol \Omega \sigma^2_e\right)
$$

-   [Prediction of new environments]{.green}

## Reaction norm models {.custom1}

> "*The ECs may not fully describe differences across environments, perhaps because some relevant ECs were not measured or because of model miss-specification (e.g., non-linear effects of ECs on the trait of interest). Similarly, because of imperfect linkage disequilibrium (LD) between markers and genes at causal loci or because of model misspecification (e.g., interactions between alleles that are unaccounted for), the regression on markers may not fully describe genetic differences among lines.*"
> --- @jarquin_reaction_2014


## Reaction norm models {.custom1}


-   "Residual" environmental effects:

$$
\bar{\boldsymbol y} = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol Z_1 \boldsymbol \omega + \boldsymbol Z_2 \boldsymbol e + \boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol g + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

$$
\boldsymbol e \sim \mathcal{N} \left(\boldsymbol 0, \boldsymbol I \sigma^2_e\right)
$$

. . .

-   What about the "residual" genetic effects?

## Reaction norm models {.custom1}

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
**Genotype-by-environmic marker interaction** (first order multiplicative interaction)

$$
gw_{ik} = g_i \times \omega_k
$$
:::

. . .

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
$$
\operatorname{Cov} \left(gw_{ik}, gw_{i^\prime k^\prime}\right) = G_{ii^\prime} \times \Omega_{kk^\prime}
$$
:::

. . .

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
-   Interaction built with the cell-by-cell (Hadamard) product between the entries of $\boldsymbol G$ and $\boldsymbol \Omega$
:::

. . . 

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
$$
\bar{\boldsymbol y} = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol Z_1 \boldsymbol \omega + \boldsymbol Z_2 \boldsymbol e + \boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol g + \boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol {g\omega} + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$
:::

. . .

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
$$
\boldsymbol {g\omega} \sim \mathcal{N} \left[\boldsymbol 0, \left(\boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol G \boldsymbol Z_3^\prime\right) \odot \left(\boldsymbol Z_1 \boldsymbol \Omega \boldsymbol Z_1^\prime\right) \sigma^2_{g\omega}\right]
$$

:::

## Reaction norm models {.custom1}

**Genotype-by-environment interaction**

$$
\bar{\boldsymbol y} = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol Z_1 \boldsymbol \omega + \boldsymbol Z_2 \boldsymbol e + \boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol g + \boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol {g\omega} + \boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol {ge} + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

. . .

$$
\boldsymbol {ge} \sim \mathcal{N} \left[\boldsymbol 0, \left(\boldsymbol Z_3 \boldsymbol G \boldsymbol Z_3^\prime\right) \odot \left(\boldsymbol Z_2  \boldsymbol Z_2^\prime\right) \sigma^2_{ge}\right]
$$

-   "Residual" genotype-by-environment interaction
